item.title: Puget Audio Taps Future Present Labs for Manufacturing Partnership
item.description:
SEATTLE, WA — February 16, 2026 — Puget Audio, a Seattle-based boutique builder of analog FX pedals and Eurorack modules, has tapped Future Present Labs to handle manufacturing support for their debut product line.

Puget Audio designs handwired analog pedals and modular synth hardware: no DSP, no modeling, just discrete circuitry and premium components. Their first pedal designs cover the essentials: overdrive, fuzz, and analog delay. They also needed short-run Eurorack panels cut cleanly and locally as module designs move through prototype and first-article builds.

item.title: Announcing AgentRFQ: An Open Standard for Agent-to-Manufacturer Requests
item.description:
Today we’re releasing AgentRFQ 1.0.0 — an open JSON standard for AI agents to request manufacturing quotes from human-approved fulfillment workflows.

GitHub: https://github.com/FuturePresentLabs/AgentRFQ

The Problem

Agents are getting good at generating CAD. They can produce STL files, write parametric scripts, even optimize topology. But the gap between “I have a 3D model” and “I have a part” is still wide.

Most agent workflows break at the handoff:

  • Files without context — An STL tells you nothing about tolerances, material, or quantity
  • Missing constraints — Critical fits get lost in translation
  • Process confusion — Should this be 3D printed? Machined? Cast?
  • No validation — Bad inputs waste everyone’s time

The result? Agents that can design but can’t deliver. Humans spending hours clarifying what should have been explicit.

item.title: Agentic Manufacturing: The JARVIS Moment (and how to actually get parts made)
item.description:
There’s a scene in Iron Man that keeps coming back to me: Tony Stark walks into his lab, throws a switch, and says something like “wake up, daddy’s home.” The room comes alive. Systems spin up. Tools become extensions of intent. Hardware becomes fast.

That’s the real promise of agentic computing, at least to me. Not just better text. Not just tokens and internet points. The inflection point is the JARVIS moment: when an agent can help build real hardware that feels impossible until it’s done.

item.title: C7 Bellevue Taps FPL for Custom Parts Across Its Flagship Event Venue
item.description:
SEATTLE, WA – November 15, 2025 – Future Present Labs has begun fabricating custom components for C7 Belevue, a luxury Bellevue event space undergoing ongoing interior updates.

The current scope includes custom light fixture housings, machined metal keepsakes, and architectural shrouds designed to conceal reconfigured equipment mounting points while maintaining the venue’s aesthetic.

“Event spaces need hardware that looks intentional but can take a beating,” said Avery Wagar, CEO of Future Present Labs. “We’re working directly with C7’s team to prototype and produce pieces that fit their operational reality—quick turnarounds, field-adjustable designs, and finishes that don’t look like afterthoughts.”

item.title: Daisy Patch PCB Prototyping
item.description:
Daisy Patch PCB Prototyping

Future Present Labs helps builders prototype Daisy Patch and Daisy-based Eurorack hardware. We support PCB revisions, control layouts, panel fit, carrier boards, test fixtures, and the practical bring-up work required to turn a digital audio idea into a module people can patch.

Daisy Patch projects sit at the intersection of firmware, audio electronics, controls, and mechanical packaging. The PCB has to expose the right knobs, jacks, switches, and debug access while fitting behind a panel and inside a case. Getting that right early saves painful board spins.

item.title: Daisy Seed Carrier Board Design
item.description:
Daisy Seed Carrier Board Design

Future Present Labs designs and prototypes Daisy Seed carrier boards for audio hardware teams building synth modules, effects pedals, controllers, test fixtures, and embedded DSP products. Daisy is powerful because it gets audio firmware moving quickly; the carrier board is where that firmware becomes a usable piece of hardware.

A good Daisy Seed carrier board is not just a breakout. It has to support the controls, audio I/O, power, mechanical mounting, panel layout, debugging access, and eventual enclosure or module format. We help bridge the gap between firmware experimentation and a board that can survive real testing.

item.title: Electronics Prototyping Seattle

Electronics prototypes rarely fail in only one way. A schematic issue may look like firmware. A firmware issue may look like a sensor problem. A connector placed in the wrong spot can make a good board hard to use. We help work through those practical edges.

We are most useful when the prototype crosses domains. A machined part may need a board mount. A PCB may need a fixture. A firmware test may need a repeatable sensor position. A customer demo may need enough polish to be trusted without pretending it is final production.

item.title: Eurorack Cases

Eurorack cases are structural, electrical, and ergonomic products at the same time. Rails need to align, modules need clearance, power access needs to be sensible, and the case has to survive real patching without flexing or fighting the user. We help turn case concepts into buildable parts.

item.title: Eurorack Panel Fabrication Seattle
item.description:

We support flat panel cutting, hole cleanup, engraving, revision marks, and the mechanical details that determine whether a module feels solid once it is mounted in a case.

Eurorack panels look simple until the stackup is wrong. Pot shafts, jack nuts, LED pipes, standoffs, PCB headers, rail clearance, and silkscreen or engraving locations all compete for space. We help review those constraints before cutting so a panel is not just pretty, but usable.

item.title: Fixture Design Seattle
item.description:
Fixture Design in Seattle

Future Present Labs designs and builds fixtures in Seattle for machining, inspection, assembly, electronics testing, and repeatable prototype work. A good fixture makes the next operation faster, safer, and easier to verify.

Fixtures are how small teams buy repeatability. They locate parts the same way, protect delicate features, reduce operator judgment, and make test data easier to trust. They do not need to be elaborate; they need to remove the right uncertainty.

item.title: Guitar Pedal Enclosure Machining
item.description:
Guitar Pedal Enclosure Machining

Future Present Labs machines and marks guitar pedal enclosures for boutique builders, prototype runs, and early production batches. We support common pedal enclosure workflows such as 125B drilling and milling, jack and switch layouts, pot holes, LED holes, battery or board clearance, laser engraving, and assembly-aware fixture work.

Pedal enclosures are small, but the details matter. A switch hole that is slightly off, a jack layout that fights the PCB, or labels that do not survive handling can slow a launch. We help line up the mechanical work with the circuit, artwork, wiring, and assembly plan.

item.title: Hardware Prototyping Seattle

The best hardware prototype is not necessarily the prettiest one. It is the one that exposes risk: fit, thermal behavior, signal integrity, cable routing, mounting, assembly access, power, firmware behavior, or test repeatability.

item.title: Laser Engraving Seattle
item.description:
Laser Engraving in Seattle

Future Present Labs provides MOPA fiber laser engraving and marking in Belltown, Seattle for prototypes, parts, panels, small batches, and production support. Engraving is useful when labels need to survive handling, cleaning, assembly, or field use.

A MOPA fiber laser gives more control over pulse settings than a basic marking setup, which can help with contrast, heat input, and mark quality on metals and some coated or engineered surfaces. The right settings still depend on material, finish, coating, desired contrast, and whether the mark is decorative or functional.

item.title: Part Marking Seattle
item.description:

Industrial marking is different from decoration. The mark needs to be readable after handling, cleaning, assembly, and sometimes coating or field use. That means placement, contrast, size, orientation, and material all matter.

item.title: Prototype Machining Seattle
item.description:
Prototype Machining in Seattle

Prototype machining is different from production machining. The goal is to make the next test possible, learn quickly, and avoid spending time on details that do not affect the current decision. Future Present Labs helps Seattle teams machine prototype parts with that mindset.

A prototype may need production-like material, real threads, bearing fits, flatness, or stiffness. It may also only need to prove clearance, ergonomics, assembly sequence, or sensor placement. The process should match the question the prototype is supposed to answer.

item.title: Waterjet Cutting Seattle
item.description:
Waterjet Cutting in Seattle

Future Present Labs supports WAZER abrasive waterjet cutting in Belltown, Seattle for teams that need accurate flat-pattern parts without heat-affected edges. Waterjet cutting is useful for metals, plastics, composites, rubber, gasket stock, and other materials where laser heat or mechanical cutting is a poor fit.

The WAZER is a compact abrasive waterjet platform, which makes it a strong fit for prototypes, short-run flat parts, panels, shims, gaskets, brackets, and blanks that later receive CNC finishing. It is not the right tool for every large-format or heavy-plate job; when scale or thickness exceeds the sensible range, we can help identify that early.
